What the stranger did to help
How it changed the way you see strangers

phrases.meaning: help me in a difficult moment
somewhere far from towns or people
help others because someone helped you

model: I'm going to talk about a man who helped me when my motorbike broke down on a trip to Ha Giang two years ago. I was riding with a friend on a mountain road, which was really beautiful but pretty much in the middle of nowhere, and suddenly the engine just died. There was no phone signal, it was getting dark, and honestly we were completely at a loss. Then, out of the blue, an older man who was driving a small truck stopped next to us. He didn't speak much, but he looked at the bike, shook his head, and lifted it onto the back of his truck. He drove us about fifteen kilometres to a tiny village where his cousin had a repair shop, and he waited there until it was fixed. When we tried to give him some money, he refused to take anything and just smiled and drove off. I never even found out his name. It was such a random act of kindness, and he really came to our rescue, because I have no idea what we would have done otherwise. I think the experience restored my faith in people, since you often hear stories about strangers who try to cheat tourists. Now I'm trying to pay it forward. Whenever I see someone who's struggling on the street, like a tourist who's lost or a driver with a flat tyre, I stop and ask if they need help.
